title: search/list: add --long flag to show full chunk content
description: The plain-text output of 'search' and 'list' currently truncates chunk content to a single line with '...'. Add a --long flag to both subcommands that prints the full content of each result, clearly delimited (e.g. a separator line between results). Without --long, keep the current compact format. Update the argparse help text for both subcommands to document the flag. No changes to --json output.

handoff_summary.completed: Added --long argparse flag to search and list subcommands; updated cmd_search and cmd_list to branch on args.long with full-content + delimiter output; --json path unchanged; syntax verified with py_compile; committed.
handoff_summary.risks: None identified — purely additive flag with no effect on existing output modes.
handoff_summary.next_action: Run tester agent to validate --long flag behaviour for search and list.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None — only memory.py modified; no overlap with other in-flight beads expected.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Delimiter format uses --- as prefix/suffix with metadata inline (distance, id, source, date) so the header is self-contained per result. Blank line after each block improves readability when multiple results are shown.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Tests should cover: search --long prints full content and separator; list --long prints full content and separator; search without --long still truncates; list without --long still truncates; --json unchanged by --long.

conflict_risks: None — only memory.py modified; no overlap with other in-flight beads expected.

execution_history.summary: Added --long flag to both search and list subcommands. When set, each result is printed with a full-content block preceded by a delimiter header line (--- [dist] id (source: ...) --- for search; --- id (source: ...) date --- for list) and followed by a blank line. Without --long, compact truncated output is unchanged. --json output is unaffected. Argparse help text updated for both subcommands.
